paper.title: Pure Exploration for Constrained Best Mixed Arm Identification with a Fixed Budget

settings.name_in_paper: Constrained best mixed arm identification (CBMAI) with a fixed budget
unmapped: Each pull returns a reward and L cost samples (vector-valued Gaussian observation)
Goal is to identify the support (optimal LP basis, including slack variables) of the best mixed arm maximizing expected reward subject to L linear expected-cost constraints c p <= c_bar
Means of arms K_0+1..K are known to the learner; only first K_0 arms are unknown
Budget N is the total number of samples (mapped to T)
Assumption 1: the LP has a unique optimal solution with exactly L+1 nonzero coordinates (nondegenerate)
settings.definition_quote: We would like to determine a mixed arm $p^*$ ... $\max_{p\in \distset_K}\{\mathbf{r}^T p : \mathbf{c} p \leq \costbound \}$ ... receives a reward $R_a \sim \mathcal{N}(r_a, \sigma_r^2)$, and also incurs costs $C_{l,a} \sim \mathcal{N}(c_{l,a}, \sigma_c^2)$ ... We consider a fixed-budget setting, i.e., we can only obtain at most $N$ such samples ... minimizes the misidentification probability $\Pr_{\mathbf{r},\mathbf{c}}(\armset^{\mathrm{\phi}} \neq \mathcal{I}^*)$

settings.name_in_paper: CBMAI with a fixed budget, all arms unknown, known variances (lower bound)
unmapped: Each pull returns a reward and L cost samples (vector-valued Gaussian observation)
Goal is to identify the optimal LP basis (support) of the best constrained mixed arm, or output empty set if infeasible
Budget N is the total number of samples (mapped to T)
Instance class: infeasible instances or instances satisfying Assumption 1 (unique nondegenerate LP optimum)
settings.definition_quote: We consider a class of instances with Gaussian rewards and costs such that the variances $\sigma_c^2, \sigma_r^2$ are fixed and known ... For simplicity, we consider $K_0 = K$, i.e., all arms are unknown. We define $\varTheta$ to be a class of instances $\theta$ that either (i) has no feasible solution, or (ii) satisfies Assumption 1.

algorithms.name: Score Function-based Successive Reject (SFSR) with intersection value score

symbols.L: number of cost constraints (treated as constant in O_L)
symbols.K_0: number of arms with unknown means
symbols.N_tilde: (T - K_0)/(3*((L+1)/2 + log(K_0))), T being the budget N
symbols.G_min: min_{2<=i<=K} Delta_(i+L)^2 / i, with Delta_(k) the k-th smallest arm value gap

conditions: Assumption 1: the LP has a unique optimal solution with exactly L+1 non-zero coordinates
Gaussian rewards and costs with variances sigma_r^2, sigma_c^2

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Let $\armset^{\fcnm}$ denote the output of Algorithm \ref{algo:ivsr}. Then, under Assumption \ref{assump:unique}, we have $\Pr(\armset^{\fcnm} \neq \mathcal{I}^* ) \leq \bigO_L(K)\cdot \exp(-\Tilde{N} \Delta_0^{2}/ K ) + \bigO_L(K^{L+2}) \cdot\exp(-\min_{2\leq i\leq K}\Tilde{N}\Delta_{(i+L)}^2 /i )$ where $\Tilde{N} := \frac{N - K_0}{3(\frac{L+1}{2} + \log K_0)}$

results.notes: Budget N mapped to T. Big-O treats L as constant (O_L). Algorithm needs known arms' means and cost bounds but not variances. Paper also derives a liminf error-exponent consequence (eq. ub-sfsr).

symbols.Delta_L2: Delta_(L+2), the smallest nonzero arm value gap

conditions: Gaussian rewards and costs with known variances

source.label: prop:lowerbound
source.quote: For any consistent algorithm $\phi_N$, under any instance $\theta$ satisfying Assumption \ref{assump:unique}, the mis-identification probability satisfies $\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty} -\dfrac{1}{N} \log\Pr_{\theta}(\mathcal{X}^{\phi_N} \neq \mathcal{I}^{\theta}) \leq \dfrac{1}{2}\min\{\Delta_0^2, \Delta_{(L+2)}^2\}.$

results.notes: Bound is on the error exponent (limsup of -(1/N) log P(error)); the expression records the exponent, i.e. P(error) >= exp(-N*(exponent + o(1))).

symbols.Delta_L2: Delta_(L+2), the smallest nonzero arm value gap

conditions: applies only to the USLP algorithm (uniform sampling then solve empirical LP)
Gaussian rewards and costs with known variances

source.label: prop:lowerbound
source.quote: Furthermore, for the \texttt{USLP} algorithm, we have $\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty} -\dfrac{1}{N} \log\Pr_{\theta}(\mathcal{X}^{\mathrm{USLP}_N} \neq \mathcal{I}^{\theta}) \leq \dfrac{1}{2K}\min\{\Delta_0^2, \Delta_{(L+2)}^2\}$

results.notes: Lower bound on the error probability of the specific USLP baseline (upper bound on its error exponent).
